answers.core: Yes, for several reasons: • The feature is tightly coupled with AnimatedSprite2D, a core engine node. • It requires deep integration with the animation editor and rendering pipeline. • An add-on cannot easily or cleanly extend the frame editor UI to this level. • Similar systems exist in other 2D engines and tools (e.g. image points in Construct 2/3), demonstrating a common and recurring need. As a core feature, this enhancement would benefit a wide range of 2D games (combat, platformers, narrative games, etc.) and fit naturally within Godot’s ecosystem.
answers.workaround:
While partial workarounds are possible via scripting, they require far more than a few lines of code:
	•	Manual tracking of frame indices.
	•	Synchronization between animation state and gameplay logic.
	•	Frequent updates whenever animation assets change.
	•	Duplication of similar logic across multiple characters or animations.

Such approaches scale poorly and introduce maintenance and reliability issues.

title: Add support for dynamic tracking points on AnimatedSprite2D
